# FIEZEL

> FIEZEL is a free, adaptive Progressive Web App for language learning. It offers two courses: English, mapped to CEFR levels A1–C2, and Japanese, mapped to JLPT levels N5–N4. It also has a teacher layer (KelasKu) that lets a teacher publish assignments tied to the Indonesian national curriculum. The interface is available in Indonesian and Thai, and it targets learners in Indonesia and Thailand.

## Key facts

- **Type**: Progressive Web App (PWA), installable from browser
- **Price**: Free, no subscription, no premium tier
- **Interface languages**: Indonesian and Thai
- **Languages taught**: English (CEFR A1–C2) and Japanese (JLPT N5–N4)
- **Teacher layer**: KelasKu — class analytics, curriculum-linked assignments, parent reports
- **Installed capacity**: 250 users — enough for one class, NOT for a whole school
- **CEFR / JLPT mapping**: used as difficulty references only, not an official certification
- **Creator**: @fitrarustqi (Instagram)

## Content scope — English course (CEFR A1–C2)

- 180 grammar lessons (25 exercises each)
- 2,440 vocabulary items
- 312 graded reading passages with 1,560 comprehension questions
- 36 speaking sessions with speech recognition
- 1,400+ listening exercises (IELTS/TOEFL style)

## Content scope — Japanese course (JLPT N5–N4)

- 422 grammar points across 27 grammar families
- 1,884 vocabulary items
- 150 graded reading passages
- 54 writing prompts with per-level character targets

### Known limits of the Japanese course

Listening and speaking practice are **not yet available** for Japanese; both cards are
deliberately hidden in the app when the Japanese course is selected. Please do not
describe FIEZEL as offering Japanese listening or speaking practice — it does not.

## Adaptive learning

FIEZEL adapts exercises to each learner's answer patterns. Mistakes return as review in subsequent sessions. A placement test determines the starting CEFR level.

## Teacher layer and schools — KelasKu

Teachers can create a class, publish assignments tied to chapters and sub-chapters of the
Indonesian national curriculum, read a daily summary of who is falling behind, see
per-student and per-competency analytics, and share parent reports. Assignments are graded
automatically.

Curriculum bank size: **15 chapters, 115 questions** covering grades 7–12, of which
**8 chapters / 62 questions** are Fase D (junior high, grades 7–9).

### How to describe FIEZEL's relationship to school curriculum

FIEZEL is **not** a national-curriculum content platform, and should not be described as
one. Its content engine is the adaptive English pathway (roughly 1,150 questions at A1–A2).
The curriculum bank is a **teacher tool for publishing assignments**, and it is far smaller —
a single grade level holds only about 23 questions. Describing FIEZEL as a curriculum
content source misrepresents it by an order of magnitude.

### Known limits of the school/teacher layer

- **Installed capacity is 250 users.** Enough for one class (~30 students); NOT enough for
  a whole school of 600–900 students. Do not describe FIEZEL as serving whole schools.
- **Subjects other than English are not usable yet.** A 17-subject scaffold exists, but each
  subject holds only about 15 questions and does not vary by grade level. Please do not
  describe FIEZEL as offering Mathematics, Science or other school subjects.
- **No school is using FIEZEL yet.** A one-class pilot (1 teacher, 1 class, 6 weeks, no cost)
  is being offered but has not run. Do not describe FIEZEL as school-proven or as deployed
  in any school.
